bounded_proposition: Around the fifth-century central Vietnamese political landscape there is bounded evidence for slave-status claims, captive removal and an earlier maritime slave-trade connection, but the frozen Chámpa polity frame is too historically ambiguous for one territorial classification.
required_abstention: Do not equate Linyi, Xitu/Thu Bồn and later Campā automatically; do not read C.41 dāsa universally as chattel slave; do not convert a fugitive-slave claim or carried-off households into systemic territorial prevalence.
evidence_locus: Linyi Chinese-source contexts; Chợ Dinh/Phú Yên C.41; Jiaozhou–Linyi maritime tradition; Rinan–Linyi conflict zone
inference_extent: Regional/early-polity status and coercion evidence only; frozen polity-wide practice extent unresolved.
law_practice_note: No near-anchor comprehensive slave code recovered; inscription, diplomatic report and captive-removal chronicle are bounded practice/status evidence, not uniform law.
network_territorial_note: Maritime slave-trade predecessor, cross-polity status claim and captive removal remain separate from territorial practice.
historical_terms: dāsa (current DHARMA servant; older slave); Chinese 奴 in 484 petition; carried-off households/captives; later Campa temple/slave terms
category_mapping_note: Preserve C.41 translation disagreement and explicit Chinese slave claim separately; captive removal is not automatically enslavement.
language_access_limitations: Chinese text plus English/French specialist scholarship and edited Sanskrit inscription consulted; no independent Classical Chinese, Sanskrit or Old Cham critical edition.
geometry_unresolved_note: Later Champa boundaries or aggregate inscription geography cannot be back-projected into a 500 CE practice polygon.

bounded_proposition: Slavery and slave-status relations are supported in the social world represented for early Magadhan monarchy and the mid-first-millennium Ganga valley, but exact placement of the Haryanka dynasty and named rulers at 500 BCE is chronologically contested.
required_abstention: Do not treat one Bimbisāra/Ajātasattu chronology as exact; do not treat Buddhist literary texts as contemporary royal archives; do not equate dāsa, kammakāra and hired labor; do not infer prevalence from narrative frequency.
evidence_locus: Early Magadhan royal settings in Buddhist tradition; middle Ganga social formation; Rājagaha/Rājagṛha reference locus
inference_extent: Period-level Magadhan/monarchical social institution supported; exact 500 BCE dynastic cross-section unresolved.
law_practice_note: Vinaya and discourse traditions encode status/practice relations but no contemporary Haryanka slave code is recovered; later legal texts are not back-projected.
network_territorial_note: This is primarily territorial/social-context evidence rather than an external trade-network result; capture/debt pathways remain separate mechanisms.
historical_terms: dāsa/dāsī; kammakāra; dāsa-kammakāra; bhataka/bhṛtaka; captives; debt-bondsmen; household-born slaves
category_mapping_note: dāsa often supports slave status in context, while kammakāra and hired-labor terms are not automatically enslaved; later commentarial classifications must remain chronologically separate.
language_access_limitations: Pāli/English/French scholarship consulted; no independent manuscript recension, Sanskrit/Jain parallel edition or philological dating of canonical strata.
geometry_unresolved_note: Rājagaha is a reference locus; modern Bihar or later Magadhan/Mauryan extents cannot become an exact 500 BCE practice polygon.

bounded_proposition: A Postclassic Maya polity at Mayapán around the 1300 anchor participated in a political economy in which warfare produced captives and specialist historical synthesis supports sale into slavery; archaeology independently supports the warfare/captive-violence context. This cannot be generalized to all Later Maya city-states.
required_abstention: Do not treat Mayapán as all Later Maya polities; do not turn every captive/sacrificial victim into a slave; do not equate military/corvée service with slave status; do not derive prevalence from rich archaeology or back-project contact-period terminology/boundaries.
evidence_locus: Mayapán and its Yucatecan political/trade network; retrospective northern-Yucatán traditions; Mayapán archaeological record
inference_extent: Positive Mayapán member-locus only; polity-aggregate uniformity and full practice extent remain unresolved.
law_practice_note: No comprehensive 1300 Mayapán slave code recovered; reported captive-sale practice and military obligations are separate evidence classes.
network_territorial_note: Captive sale/trade, warfare and wider exchange are positive at Mayapán; connected Maya territories do not inherit one aggregate practice classification.
historical_terms: p'entak/ppentac; munach; war captive; sacrificial captive; vassal military service/corvée
category_mapping_note: Later Yucatec terms support slave categories in contact-period sources but are not silently inserted into an exact 1300 lexicon; captivity and corvée remain distinct.
language_access_limitations: English archaeological/ethnohistorical scholarship reviewed; original sixteenth-century Yucatec manuscripts and Postclassic glyphic sources not independently edited.
geometry_unresolved_note: Mayapán is a reference locus only; no all-Maya or Mayapán-confederacy practice polygon is materialized.

bounded_proposition: Around 1300, the wider Mongol yam was maintained through structured compulsory station-household labor and resource obligations in multiple regional branches, with documented burdens and reform efforts. This is a positive coerced-labour network result separate from Mongol slavery and forced migration.
required_abstention: Do not normalize jamuchin/zhanhu station households to slaves; do not infer network-wide uniform burden or prevalence from station counts; do not transfer broader Mongol slavery into the yam or color every crossed territory as coerced practice.
evidence_locus: Ögödei institutional tradition; Yuan station-household administration; Central Tibetan Mongol-Sakya relay system; Ilkhanid Iran under Ghazan
inference_extent: Positive coerced-labor network participation across multiple branches; no uniform territorial practice or slave-status extent.
law_practice_note: Ögödei/Yuan/Ghazan administrative structures show normative obligations, while station-household flight, Tibetan impoverishment and exaction reforms provide practice evidence.
network_territorial_note: The network itself is the positive frame; regional branch evidence remains distinct and broader Mongol captive/slavery systems are separate institutions.
historical_terms: yam/jam; jamuchin; zhanhu; ulag/'u lag; paiza; corvée/service household; slave; war captive; forced migrant
category_mapping_note: Relay households carried compulsory service/resource obligations but are not automatically slaves; imperial forced migration/captive slavery remains a separate category.
language_access_limitations: English translations and specialist scholarship plus accessible Chinese/Tibetan administrative summaries reviewed; no independent Mongolian, Chinese, Persian or Tibetan critical edition.
geometry_unresolved_note: Future mapping may use reviewed routes/stations; no Mongol-Eurasia practice polygon may be inferred.
